notes: Static table 945 publishes whole rupiah (Excel number format #\ ###\ ##0); the CSV keeps them.
Per capita values do not add across provinces; 00 is BPS's national figure from the same survey.

periods.note: One value per year. The static table's notes name Susenas Triwulan I (the first-quarter round) for 2012-2014, and the yearly tables' source lines name Susenas Maret (March) for 2017-2025; no raw file names the round for 2011, 2015 or 2016.

65.reason: Kalimantan Utara became a province in 2012; the static table prints '-' for 2011-2014 under its footnote 1), 'Data masih bergabung dengan Provinsi Kalimantan Timur' (data still combined with Kalimantan Timur)

92.reason: Papua Barat Daya became a province in 2022; the static table prints '-' for 2011-2023, and the 2023 yearly table's note says its 2023 figures still follow those of Papua Barat

95.reason: Papua Selatan became a province in 2022; the static table prints '-' for 2011-2023, and the 2023 yearly table's note says its 2023 figures still follow those of Papua

96.reason: Papua Tengah became a province in 2022; the static table prints '-' for 2011-2023, and the 2023 yearly table's note says its 2023 figures still follow those of Papua

97.reason: Papua Pegunungan became a province in 2022; the static table prints '-' for 2011-2023, and the 2023 yearly table's note says its 2023 figures still follow those of Papua

not_published.meaning: no value for the region in that year; the cell is left out, never written as 0

coverage.gaps: none: every other region, Indonesia included, has food, non_food and total in every year 2011-2025

borders: 64 (Kalimantan Timur) in 2011-2014 includes Kalimantan Utara, as the static table's footnote 1) states ('Data masih bergabung dengan Provinsi Kalimantan Timur'); 65 (Kalimantan Utara) has its own values from 2015.

91 (Papua Barat) and 94 (Papua) in 2011-2023 cover the pre-split provinces: the 2023 yearly table's note says Papua Barat Daya still follows the Papua Barat figures, and Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah and Papua Pegunungan the Papua figures. From 2024, 91 and 94 cover the post-split areas, and 92, 95, 96 and 97 start.

A per capita value of a pre-split area cannot be rebuilt from the post-split provinces without their populations, and a change from the year before across a border change compares different areas: 64 in 2015, 91 and 94 in 2024 (checks.change_not_compared).

source_priority.use: lower-priority copy, compared in checks.cross_source and never written

change_log.change: Perubahan/perbaikan angka provinsi saja (all provinsi), angka kabupaten kotanya sudah sesuai.

notes: Every value comes from static table 945, the one raw file that holds all 15 years, so the series has one source and one precision throughout. The yearly statistics tables repeat 2017-2025, with 2 decimals in 2017, 2018 and 2020-2022 and whole rupiah in 2019 and 2023-2025; every shared value agrees within 1 rupiah, and every difference is listed under checks.cross_source.

The static table rounds food, non_food and total to whole rupiah one by one, so food + non_food differs from total by up to 1 rupiah. In 2018 its totals are its rounded food plus its rounded non_food, which is why 9 totals of 2018 differ from the yearly table by more than 0.5 rupiah.

Nusa Tenggara Barat (52) in 2012: the static table prints food 291 176, non_food 234 901 and total 484 661, so food + non_food exceeds total by 41 416 rupiah. The three values are kept as published; one of them is a BPS error, and no raw file here can tell which (checks.identities, declared_breaks; checks.flags).
The 2025 yearly table is version 2, whose change log records a correction of all province figures; static table 945 (updated 2025-12-16) matches it in all 117 values of 2025.

Derived values are not stored: food share (%) = food / total x 100, and the change from the year before (%) = value in year t / value in year t-1 x 100 - 100, at current prices; the change is computed here only for the plausibility flags.

checks.flags lists every value, change and identity gap outside its range in checks.plausible_ranges for a person to review; a change flag gives the two values it compares under rupiah. A flag stays whether it reflects a real event or a source error.

identities.check: food + non_food = total, rupiah, every region and year except declared_breaks

declared_breaks.reason: BPS's own inconsistency inside static table 945, read correctly: the row's food, non_food and total cells sit in their columns and parse cleanly, and every other region and year adds up within 1 rupiah. No other raw file holds 2012, so the three values are kept as published

cross_source.check: static table 945 = yearly statistics tables, 2017-2025, rupiah
cross_source.second: statistics table, one file per year, 2 decimals (written ,00 in 2019 and 2023-2025)
cross_source.tolerance_reason: The static table rounds to whole rupiah, so a copy with 2 decimals differs by up to 0.5 rupiah; its 2018 totals are its rounded food plus its rounded non_food, which differ from the total rounded on its own by up to 1

beyond_half_rupiah.reason: 2018 totals: the static total equals the static food plus the static non_food, both already rounded (checked for each key)

cross_source.check: status: no cell of either source carries a revision marker, and no note gives a status, so every row is final

change_not_compared.reason: Kalimantan Timur: 2014 includes Kalimantan Utara, 2015 does not
Papua Barat: 2023 includes Papua Barat Daya, 2024 does not
Papua: 2023 includes Papua Selatan, Papua Tengah and Papua Pegunungan, 2024 does not

format.missing: a missing row means the source has no value; no placeholder values are written
format.layout: one value per row: key columns, then status, then value

status: final, or no marker in the source
